entities.summary:
Neferkare (b. 2700 BCE) was a naval explorer and commander of the 12th Dynasty of Ancient Egypt, active in the Global region during the Classical era. Known for his extensive maritime expeditions and diplomatic missions to neighboring civilizations.

As a key figure in the Egyptian navy, Neferkare played a crucial role in establishing trade relations with the Mycenaeans and the Hittites. His naval campaigns also helped to secure Egypt's borders against the Hyksos, a Semitic people who had invaded Egypt from the north.

Neferkare's legacy extended beyond his military conquests, as he also sponsored the construction of several temples and monuments throughout Egypt. His reign is notable for the development of a sophisticated system of record-keeping and administration, which helped to establish Egypt as a major power in the ancient world.

Despite his significant contributions to Egyptian history, Neferkare remains a relatively unknown figure outside of Egyptological circles. However, his impact on the development of Egyptian civilization and his place in the broader history of the ancient Near East are undeniable.

The discovery of the Neferkare Stela, a monumental stone slab discovered in the 19th century, provided valuable insights into the life and achievements of this enigmatic figure. The stela, which features an image of Neferkare in military regalia, offers a unique glimpse into the culture and politics of ancient Egypt during the 12th Dynasty.
